topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Concept of 'Perspective' (Prerequisite Review)
sections.content: Recall that a basis is a set of 'coordinate axes' (basis vectors). Explain that a vector exists independently, but its coordinates depend on the chosen basis. Use a visual of a point in 2D space described by (x, y) relative to standard grid lines.
sections.example: Imagine a robot looking at a fruit bowl. If the robot moves, its 'forward' and 'right' axes shift. The fruit's location remains the same, but the coordinate numbers change.

sections.title: Visualizing the Basis Transformation
sections.content: Introduce two bases: Basis B (standard, e.g., i, j) and Basis C (custom, e.g., v1, v2). Use an animation where the grid lines warp from square (standard) to slanted/stretched (new basis). Emphasize that the space hasn't changed, only the ruler we use to measure it.
sections.example: Representing a vector v=[3, 2] in the standard grid, then overlaying a new red grid (Basis C) to see how those same coordinates translate into new numbers [a, b].

sections.title: The Change-of-Basis Matrix
sections.content: Introduce the Transition Matrix (P). Explain that P maps coordinates from Basis C to Basis B. Show the matrix construction: columns are the coordinates of the new basis vectors expressed in the old basis.
sections.example: If Basis C is defined by vectors v1=[1, 1] and v2=[-1, 1], the matrix P = [[1, -1], [1, 1]] acts as a 'translator' for any coordinate pair.

sections.title: The Formula and Application
sections.content: Present the core equation: [v]_B = P[v]_C. Explain that to go the other way, we need the inverse matrix (P^-1). Connect this to real-world navigation systems.
sections.example: A GPS satellite uses a global basis, but a self-driving car uses its own local 'body-centric' basis. The car uses a change-of-basis matrix to convert global coordinates into its own local 'drive-straight-ahead' instructions.

Vectors exist independently of our chosen basis.
Coordinates depend entirely on that chosen basis.

Grid lines warp to represent the new basis.

storyboard.title: The Change-of-Basis Matrix
lecture_lines: The transition matrix maps between different bases.
Construct columns from new basis vectors.
It acts as a translator for coordinates.

Show matrix multiplication action on arbitrary vector x.

storyboard.title: The Formula and Application
lecture_lines: Inverse matrices reverse the coordinate conversion.
This powers systems like self-driving car navigation.
